parts.why: Form B (2 + 3 = 5) is the same fact as form A (3 + 2 = 5), so B asks exactly what A asks. Form A also has the answer 5 in part 1 and again in part 2 (8 - 3 = 5). Change B to another sum within 10, e.g. 'Hugo räknar 4 citroner. Hugo hittar 3 citroner till.' (= 7), and keep A part 2 or change A part 1 to 3 + 4 = 7 so A does not repeat 5. Wording: 'Elias räknar 3 fikon' is an odd opening for a story; 'Elias har 3 fikon. Han hittar 2 fikon till.' is how a Swedish teacher tells it.
8 - 3 and 9 - 2, one right answer each (see part 1 about the repeated 5 in form A).

Box 2 is identical in A and B (6 into 2 boxes = 3). Form A has two 2-box shares, form B has one 3-box share (6 limes, answer 2) and one 2-box share, so B is harder. Give both forms one 2-box and one 3-box card with different totals, e.g. A: 8 into 2 (4) and 9 into 3 (3); B: 10 into 2 (5) and 6 into 3 (2). Direction: the pictures stand in a row, not a 'hög', and 'var och en' means people; say 'Dela bilderna lika i lådorna. Skriv hur många det blir i varje låda.'
4 + 4 = 8 and 6 + 3 = 9, natural Swedish, one answer.

Each card shows one picture and two boxes, and one box is labelled with the SAME picture (bat to the bat box, penguin to the penguin box, apricot to the apricot box, cherry to the cherry box). That is matching identical pictures, not 'Sortera efter sort'. Label the boxes with a category and give a different member, e.g. boxes 'djur' (a dog) and 'frukt' (an apple), item a bat; or boxes 'flyger' (a bird) and 'simmar' (a fish), item a penguin. (The cherry and the apricot also look like an apple and an orange; with category boxes that no longer matters.)
glad - ledsen and varm - kall, the distractors (långsam, vinter, lätt, natt) are not opposites of the word. One right answer.
Enlarged both: A (blank paper, flower, flower + text, envelope) and B (fence painted bit by bit) each have one order. Direction says 'i varje berättelse' for one story; see instruction.
Three targets per card, all found. Small imbalance: A 'o' has the look-alikes å and ä in the row, B 'c' and 'u' have none; consider an 'o'/'e' near the c in B.

B card 1 (C to c) is the same shape in two sizes, so a child matches it without knowing the letter; A has L-l and R-r, where the shapes differ. Replace C with a letter whose small form looks different, e.g. 'E -> e' or 'G -> g'. Also, the card shows the big letter, an arrow and three small letters in a row, and the key rings the answer; a line drawn from L to l would cross the other letters. Say 'Ringa in den lilla bokstaven som hör ihop med den stora.'

Direction says 'skriv sedan en egen på den tomma raden', but there is no empty line: the child writes at the free end of the same line. Say 'Skriv sedan en egen bokstav i slutet av raden.' R and Ö (A) against O and K (B) are even.
val (whale) and kiwi (fruit), clear pictures, the word is given to trace.
i j / m p / q r / w x all correct in the Swedish alphabet. 'för att göra alfabetet färdigt' is an English pattern; see instruction.

gryta 2, lemonad 3, val 1 / matlåda 3, ros 1, panda 2, all correct when the teacher says the word (as the teacher page asks). Make that explicit in the direction: 'Lyssna när jag säger ordet. Skriv hur många stavelser du hör.'

Form A card 1 'ängel' keyed 'Ä': the first sound of ängel is short [ɛ], which Swedish children hear exactly like short e (engelsk, eld). A child who writes E has heard correctly and is marked wrong. Replace with a word whose first sound has one spelling, e.g. 'orm' (O), 'mus' (M) or 'sol' (S). The other five (hand H, ben B, räv R, docka D, igloo I) are fine when the teacher says the word; a child naming the leg alone might say 'knä'.

kort t, skrivbord d, bi i / trollstav v, jordglob b, tiger r are all the last letter. kort and skrivbord end in the retroflex rt/rd sound; a child still writes t and d, so I accept them, but 'bok' (k) and 'sol' (l) would be cleaner for a lesson about the LAST SOUND.
kamel 5, fisk 4 / varg 4 (v-a-r-j), sebra 5. If a child calls the wolf 'hund', that is also 4 sounds. A and B even.

Both forms still test only PÅ, the easiest word, in a lesson about på, under, bredvid, vänster och höger. Add a second card to each form asking UNDER (A) and BREDVID (B), or the same two words with new pictures in both forms, with the word read by the teacher: 'Ringa in bilden som är UNDER lådan.' The pictures already have an item under and beside the box.
3 penguins and 3 lemons, all ringed. Direction wording, see instruction.
Largest fox (3rd) and largest papaya (1st) clearly biggest.
Form B still stands in pure falling order (3, 2, 1): the apples make a staircase, so B is easier than A (3, 1, 2). Shuffle B, e.g. small, big, middle (1, 3, 2) or middle, small, big (2, 1, 3).
panda heavier than duck, mango heavier than strawberry. The square frame only appears in the key; the check shows two circles.
AB patterns of 8, the 9th is the first picture; answer in different places in A and B.
Counted: 9 iguanas, 6 tigers, 10 raspberries, 5 figs.
Colour 3 parrots / 4 pears of 8; the key note that any 3 (4) count is right.

Measured on the PDF: the 5 tigers in A are 20 pt (7 mm) and the 4 pandas 25 pt, in one long row; B's 6 kiwis are about 11 mm and stand as 3 + 3. A quick look at 7 mm pictures in a line of 5 is harder than a 3 + 3 pattern. Draw A's pictures at B's size and give the 5 a pattern (3 + 2 or dice five), or put B's 6 in a single row.
8 vs 6 owls and 6 vs 7 bananas, one group has more.
Direction says 'Skriv den sedan själv i den tomma rutan', but there is no box, only the free end of the line. Say 'Skriv den sedan själv i slutet av raden.' 7, 2 / 8, 1 are even.
Counted: antelopes 5, orangutans 3, pandas 5; bananas 5, pineapples 4, lemons 3.
Bars 4/3 and 4/1 read correctly (B's 'plum' looks like an apple, but the child reads the bar for the picture). 'Skriv dess tal' is stiff; see instruction for G1-143.
23 sheep, best guess 25 of 10/25; 15 avocados, 15 of 15/30.
4 + 3 = 7 camels, 2 + 6 = 8 blueberries.
5 = 3 + 2 and 5 = 1 + 4; 'femkamrat' is the school word.

Form A card 2 (söndag) asks the child to go over the end of the week (i morgon = måndag; the Swedish week starts on Monday); form B (tisdag, fredag) never crosses it, so B is easier. Give B a card over the week boundary too, e.g. 'måndag' (i går söndag, i morgon tisdag). Also: the writing box is about 4.9 cm with an 8 mm line for 'torsdag'/'måndag' in first-grade handwriting; make the boxes wider. In the key the answer word sits on top of the line and touches the right edge.

Three of four blanks are the same in A and B (2:a, 3:e, 5:e; only 8:e/7:e differ), so B asks almost exactly what A asks. Give B other given places, e.g. given 1:a, 3:e, 5:e, 8:e; missing 2:a, 4:e, 6:e, 7:e. The abbreviations 1:a, 2:a, 3:e are correct Swedish.

At 12:00 both hands lie on top of each other on 12, so the teacher cannot see whether the child knows which hand is which; 6:00 is a straight vertical line. B has 2:00 and 10:00, where both hands are visible. Change A to e.g. 4:00 and 8:00. The key writes '12:00' in small orange text in the clock face instead of drawing the hands; draw them in the key.
13 - 3 = 10 and 14 - 2 = 12, rows line up one to one. Direction says 'fler eller färre' and 'varje räknehändelse' where the card asks only 'fler' in one story; see instruction.

The direction asks for a question mark in the block model for the missing number, but the key fills the part with the answer (16 / 9 / 7) and gives only '16 - 9 = 7'. Show '?' in the key's block model (or note that the solved number is also accepted) and accept '16 - 7 = 9' (B: '13 - 7 = 6'), which a child writes just as often. Both stories cross ten; A and B even.

4 + 12 = 16 and 14 + 5 = 19. Add to the key that any question that can be answered from the story counts (e.g. 'Hur många fler äpplen lade Ebba dit?' = 8). 'Om frågan saknas' sounds as if some stories have a question; see instruction.

Form A part 4 is 4 + 12 = 16, exactly the sum of form A part 3 (4 + 12 = 16): the child can copy the answer. Change A part 4, e.g. 'Astrid hittar 6 päron på morgonen och 9 päron på eftermiddagen' (= 15). B (10 + 7) is fine; 'mangos' is everyday speech, 'mangor' or another fruit reads better in a school text.

Same defect as the förskoleklass sorting part: the picture (swan, pig, strawberry, blackberry) goes to the box labelled with the identical picture. That is picture matching, below åk 1, not sorting into three groups. Label the three boxes with categories (e.g. 'flyger', 'simmar', 'går', or fruit colours röd, gul, grön) shown by other members, and give an item that is not one of the labels.
8 and 5 / 9 and 4 tally marks, bundles of five correct in the key.
1 moose, 6 penguins / 6 nectarines, 5 bananas counted.
6/5 and 6/1 read correctly. Small note: 6 is an answer in both part 3 and part 4 of each form; vary one (e.g. 7 and 4).
2 + 6 = 8 and 3 + 6 = 9; the equation is printed so the dots are only support.
Now 9 - 7 = 2 and 10 - 4 = 6, crossed-out pictures counted correctly. Level fits åk 1.

All six colours in the key are right, but form A has four subtractions and two additions while form B has one subtraction and five additions (including 4 + 6 and 6 + 4 side by side), so B is easier. Swap two of B's additions for subtractions with the same results, e.g. '0 + 3' -> '8 - 5' and '4 + 3' -> '9 - 2'.
8 - 2 = 6 and 10 - 2 = 8, same story shape in both forms.
4 + 5, 7 - 2 / 8 + 2, 6 - 4; one addition and one subtraction in each form.
Arrow positions measured on the sheet: 3, 8, 19 and 6, 9, 13 are exact.

The direction 'Fyll i alla rutor på sidan' names the page, but the boxes are in one card; say 'Fyll i alla tomma rutor.' Answers (15/17, 1 tiotal 6 ental, 26, 6; 18/20, 1 9, 29, 9) are right. Note that '10 mer' leads to 26 and 29, above the unit's 0-20.
sexton among sjutton/femton, nio among elva/tio; femton, åtta among arton/sex. Good traps.
6 + 6, 4 + 4 / 7 + 7, 3 + 3 even. The vultures are very small but the sum is printed. 'Hälften' from the lesson title is never asked.

Checked the student form: the pictures stand in pairs and the leftover one sits alone in an orange dashed frame, while the direction says 'Om en blir över är talet udda.' The card therefore gives the answer away: a framed lone picture means 'udda'. Remove the sentence with the rule from the direction and do not frame the leftover (let it stand at the end of the row). Also, A and B both go udda-jämnt in the same order.
Counted: 18 donkeys = 9 par jämnt, 11 rabbits = 5 par udda, 12 pineapples = 6 par, 17 apples = 8 par udda.
mun, mus, paj / fot, kam, lim; the three letters allow only these words for the pictures.
Now even: panda 5 and gris 4 against häst 4 and tiger 5, all sound-true.
bok, får, haj / ros, gås, paj, distractors differ by one sound.

kamel, kanin / panda, delfin. Key note: 'kamäl' is not a sound-true spelling of kamel (long e and long ä are different sounds); keep only 'dälfin' for delfin as the example (short e and short ä do sound the same).
sköld-pad-da 3, tvätt-björn 2 / björn-bär 2, per-si-ka 3; the word is printed, so the apple-like peach does not matter.
tå (foot with an arrow at the big toe), kök, ben, get (with an elk as near distractor). One answer each.

Each sentence has one gap and the box holds exactly one word ('här', 'ser', 'har', 'han'), so the child only copies; nothing is read or chosen. Give two or three high-frequency words per box so reading decides, e.g. A 'här / har / hon' for 'Jag bor ___.' and B 'har / här / hon' for 'Vem ___ bollen?'.

Each card shows a picture of the answer next to the gap (rabbit -> kanin, llama -> lama, rooster -> tupp, bicycle -> cykel), so the sentence is not needed and the part repeats part 1 (word to picture). For 'Vilket ord passar i luckan?' remove the picture or show all three list words as pictures. All list words are en-words, so the article gives nothing away. 'Oscar trampar på sin cykel till skolan' reads oddly ('trampa på' = step on); say 'Oscar åker till skolan på sin ___.'

A has five word cards ('Elsa har två små leoparder.'), B only four ('Elsa har många aprikoser.'), so B is easier. Give B five, e.g. 'Elsa har tre gula aprikoser.' 'Elsa har två små leoparder' is odd; 'Elsa ser två små leoparder.' Swedish word order also allows 'Två små leoparder har Elsa.' (and 'Många aprikoser har Elsa.'); the key should accept it.

The lesson is 'vem, vad, var', but VAD is the answer on no card in either form (A: Var, Vem; B: Vem, Var). Make one card per form a vad-card, e.g. 'Olle läser en bok.' with 'en bok' marked. The pictures contradict the sentences: a doctor for 'Olle läser på lekplatsen', a farmer for 'Hugo sover', a construction worker for 'Nils läser på stranden'; remove them or show what the sentence says.
Enlarged: paper strips -> cut -> chain -> full chain; paper -> pieces -> mosaic fish -> finished fish. One answer each, the other two options are the first picture again and an unrelated scene.
Hexagon to the flat box, pyramid to the solid box, labels match the direction. Only one figure per form.
Enlarged: the reindeer stands at an angle, so only the bat is symmetric; in B only the blueberry seen from above.
Checked every row of Sol, Tulpan, Krabba and Paraply: the orange cells in the key mirror the teal half exactly. 25/23 against 22/20 cells.
The options are the same arrow in other directions; one matches. Easy for åk 2 but correct.

Form A asks the child to read a bundle of five (duck: five-bundle + 1 = 6); form B has only 4 and 2, no bundle. Give B a tally with a bundle, e.g. lime 7. The key shows only tiny orange numbers (4, 6) floating in the chart; draw the bars in the key.
6 turtles = 12, 4 swans = 8 / 2 clementines = 4, 7 blueberries = 14.
6 wolves = 30, 2 reindeer = 10 / 7 peaches = 35, 2 pineapples = 10.
1, 5, 2 / 5, 4, 1 correct. 'X-en' is not what children say; the lesson itself says 'kryss'. See instruction.

'Säkert' is the right answer on no row in either form (A: möjligt, möjligt, omöjligt; B: omöjligt, möjligt, möjligt), so the hardest idea of the lesson is never checked. Add a bag with one kind only (e.g. only circles: circle = säkert, star = omöjligt). 'Kryssa i en ruta' is the right Swedish way to mark a choice. 'men det måste inte hända' is not standard Swedish for 'need not'; say 'men det behöver inte hända'.

The card's reminder shows three things (Stor bokstav, Namn, Skiljetecken). A 'vi räknar åtta fiskar på bilden' has no name, B 'oscar ritar tre limer till liam' has two, so B is harder. Give A a name, e.g. 'vi räknar åtta fiskar med elsa'. 'limer' is an unusual plural; 'tre äpplen' is safer.

Answers are right (Var leker Ida? / Vem sover klockan nio? / Vem hittar tre färjor? / Var läser Leo?). But 'Olle hittar tre färjor' (finds three ferries) makes no sense; say 'Olle hittar tre fjädrar.' The pictures contradict the sentences: a waitress for 'Ida leker i skogen', a singer with a guitar for 'Nils sover'. Remove them or show the action.

One answer each, natural Swedish texts. A asks an inference (glada, because they sing), B a literal detail (en gammal kopp); acceptable, but a literal question in A or an inference in B would make them even.
uggla, räv, kanin / panda, koala, säl; all list words are en-words, so 'en' gives nothing away. 'hoar' is the right verb for an owl.

The question is 'Ben: 0 / 4 / 6' for a camel and '6 / 4 / 2' for an ostrich, and the picture shows the legs, so the child counts legs instead of reading a fact. Ask a fact the picture does not show, e.g. Kamel 'Bor i: öknen / havet / skogen', Struts 'Kan: flyga / springa fort / simma'.
en anka/and, ett bälte/skärp, en banan, ett äpple; every likely name gives the same article.
Form B has two en-words (papaya, vattenmelon) and no ett-word, so a child who writes everything under 'en' gets B fully right; A has one of each. Make B card 2 an ett-word, e.g. 'päron' or 'körsbär'.

The plural is printed in dashed letters ('valar', 'åsnor') and the child only traces it: in åk 2 that checks nothing about plural. Remove the dashed model so the child writes the plural from the singular, e.g. 'val' -> ___ with two whales.

A has two regular plurals (apor, pingviner); B has jordgubbar and the irregular 'gäss', and only B prints a hint ('gås' under the picture). Give A an irregular plural with the same hint style (e.g. 'mus' -> 'möss') or give B a regular one.

One word per form ('springa', 'avokado') is a 50 % guess, and the Verb box's icon is a running figure, so 'springa' can be matched by picture. The unit is 'Substantiv, verb och adjektiv' but no part asks for an adjective. Give each form three words, one of each class, e.g. A 'springa, boll, glad', B 'avokado, hoppa, mjuk', with the three-box layout used in the åk 3 unit.
5 tens + 6 ones = 56, 6 tens + 1 one = 61.
Now even: 70 (69/71) and 80 (79/81) both cross a ten; 35 and 36 with 10 more/less.
Arrow positions measured: 42, 54 and 46, 53.
flodhäst, jaguar, orangutang, sebra / aprikos, granatäpple, kokosnöt, äpple (ä last, good). Only B has a word with å/ä/ö; give A one too (e.g. 'älg' for 'sebra').
svag, fattig / torr, slut, each with a synonym trap. The earlier start/starta overlap is gone.
trött+sömnig, sorgsen+ledsen / välsmakande+smaskig, häpen+överraskad. Small tell: in 3 of 4 cards the two answers form a whole row.
komisk, slänga / prata, slå igen; one synonym each.
fuktig < blöt < genomblöt, snyfta < gråta < storgråta.
fisk -> fiskare (fil, fika as look-alikes), moln -> molnig (morot, moped).

One word per form ('svan', 'mjuk'), a 1-in-3 guess, and in A the word card carries a picture of a swan, which tells 'thing'. Give each form three words without pictures, one per class, e.g. A 'svan, simma, vit', B 'mjuk, kudde, sova'.

Form A asks only preteritum of two strong verbs (sov, sprang); form B asks only presens (hoppar, bär). A is much harder, and neither form checks both tenses of the lesson 'nu och i går'. Give each form one presens and one preteritum, e.g. A 'I fredags ___ Hugo hela dagen. (sova)' + 'Just nu ___ Hugo i parken. (springa)'; B 'I går ___ Elsa i parken. (hoppa)' + 'Nu ___ Maja en tung väska. (bära)'. Word order in the frames is right (V2).
A asks hon and han, B asks hon and de; only B checks the plural 'de'. Make A card 2 a pair, e.g. 'Leo och Alva' -> de, or B card 2 a single boy. Note: this part is åk 1 level for an åk 3 unit.
Hon -> Selma, Han -> Lucas / Han -> Anton, Hon -> Ester. In the key the number badges overlap the corner of the pronoun boxes; cosmetic.

sa-ll-ad and valro-ss are right. But the direction says 'Läs regeln i rutan' and the box shows only letter chips and the examples katt/boll, no rule. Either print the rule ('Efter kort vokal skriver man ofta två konsonanter.') or say 'Titta på exemplen i rutan.'
flyg and dröm are right. The direction says 'skriv ordstammen i den tomma stenen', but the answer field is a dashed rectangle, not a stone; say 'i den tomma rutan'.

Each form has ONE sentence and four words, but the direction says 'Skriv vart och ett av de fyra orden i rutorna i den mening där det passar.' Say 'Välj det ord som passar i meningen och skriv det i rutan.' Answers åhörare and vänskap are single; A's 'salongen' and 'pjäsen' are hard words for åk 3 next to B's everyday sentence.
ovanlig, oförsiktig / ohälsosam, obekväm.
dansare, sångare / lärare, städare.

Both forms have one word and it belongs to 'gå' in both (marschera, promenera); the 'titta' field is never the answer, so a child who writes everything under 'gå' is always right. Give each form two words, one per field, e.g. A 'marschera, kika', B 'promenera, stirra'. On the open question: a Swedish teacher would NOT accept 'simma' and 'klättra' under 'gå'. They are ways of moving, not ways of walking; under 'gå' belong promenera, vandra, marschera, traska, lunka, strosa, kliva, stega, trippa, smyga, stappla, lufsa. Remove simma and klättra from the gå list (or rename the field 'röra sig', which would then no longer be a word field for gå).
klagade / svarade, one fit each, Swedish quotation marks used correctly.

Both forms show one parallelogram with the answer 'inte en rektangel', and the direction's 'Kvadrater är också rektanglar' refers to a square that is not there. Give each form two or three figures, e.g. A: a square (rektangel) and a parallelogram; B: a long rectangle (rektangel) and a trapezoid.
Enlarged: one right angle per form; B's first angle is about 110 degrees, a good near miss. All right angles stand upright; one turned right angle would test more.
square 4, regular hexagon 6, ellipse 2 / equilateral triangle 3, regular star 5, isosceles trapezoid 1.
7x5 = 24, 5x3 = 16 / 8x5 = 26, 4x3 = 14; the area (35, 15, 40, 12) gives a wrong answer, good.
5 · 6 = 30, 4 · 8 = 32 match the grids.
Enlarged: A 4x2 = 8 -> 8x1 (not 3x3); B 6x2 = 12 -> 4x3 (not 2x4). Answer on the left in A, right in B.
A 4x3 (14) -> 5x2 (14, not 8x2); B 6x2 (16) -> 5x3 (16, not 3x3). The earlier position pattern is gone (A: left, right; B: right, left).

checks.why: Stories and answers are right, but B part 1 is A's fact turned round (3 + 2 / 2 + 3) and part 3 has an identical card in both forms and a harder 3-box share only in B.
Opposites and the picture series are good; the sorting part only matches identical pictures and needs category boxes.
All answers right; B's C-c is a same-shape match and two directions name an empty line or box that is not drawn.

Ruling lifted: the check now covers syllables, first, last and counted sounds fairly, and the pictures work when the teacher says the word. 'Ängel' (Ä, heard as E) must go; rhyme, the first word of the title, still has no part, so please add one when possible.
Still only PÅ in part 1, and part 4 B is still a 3-2-1 staircase; both are small changes.
Counts are right; A's quick-look pictures are half the size of B's and one direction names a box that is not there.
Every count and sum is right, A and B are even, and sorting now has its own part.
Only A crosses the week boundary, B's ordinals repeat A's blanks, and 12:00 cannot show two hands.
Good stories at the right level; form A repeats 4 + 12 = 16 in parts 3 and 4, and the key for the block model contradicts the direction.
Tally and both diagrams are right; the three-group sorting is identical-picture matching.
Levels now fit åk 1; the colour-by-code part is mostly addition in B and mostly subtraction in A.
All answers right; part 6 states the rule and frames the leftover picture, which gives the answer away.
All words are sound-true and A and B are now even; only the 'kamäl' example in the key note should change.

Ruling lifted: with six of seven lessons, including single-word reading, the check is now fair to the unit. Four parts need changes: a word choice in part 2, no answer picture in part 3, equal sentence length in part 4 and a 'vad' card in part 5.
Every answer checked, including all symmetry cells; A and B are even.
Readings are right; 'säkert' is never tested, B's tally has no bundle of five, and the key does not draw the bars.
Good texts; part 1 is uneven (names only in B), part 2 has a nonsense sentence and wrong pictures, and part 5's answer can be counted in the picture.
Part 3 is only tracing, part 2 B is all en-words, and adjectives from the title are never asked.
All answers right and part 2 is now even (70 and 80).
Every answer single and right, the earlier overlap between parts is gone.
Tense is split by form (A only past, B only present) and the word-class part has one word with a picture tell.
Answers are right, but three directions name things that are not on the card and the gå/titta part never asks 'titta'.
All numbers checked and the old position pattern is gone; part 1 is one parallelogram with the same answer in both forms.

instruction.K-642: Lyssna på räknehändelsen. Rita den i rutan. Skriv svaret.
instruction.K-639: Dela bilderna lika i lådorna. Skriv hur många det blir i varje låda.
instruction.K-042: Dra ett streck från bilden till den låda där den hör hemma.
instruction.K-351: Dra ett streck från bilden till den bild och det ord som visar motsatsen.
instruction.K-379: Titta på vad som ändras i berättelsen. Skriv 1, 2, 3 och 4 i rutorna så att bilderna kommer i rätt ordning.
instruction.K-222: Ringa in den lilla bokstaven som hör ihop med den stora.
instruction.K-238: Spåra varje bokstav. Skriv sedan en egen bokstav i slutet av raden. Börja vid den orange pricken och följ pilarna.
instruction.K-223: Skriv de bokstäver som fattas i alfabetet.
instruction.K-233: Lyssna när jag säger ordet. Skriv hur många stavelser du hör.
instruction.K-221: Lyssna när jag säger ordet. Skriv bokstaven som ordet börjar med.
instruction.K-226: Lyssna när jag säger ordet. Skriv bokstaven som ordet slutar med.
instruction.K-059: Hitta alla bilder som är likadana som den i rutan. Ringa in dem.
instruction.K-237: Spåra varje siffra. Skriv den sedan själv i slutet av raden.
instruction.G1-143: Läs av staplarna. Skriv hur många varje stapel visar.
instruction.G1-160: Dra ett streck från varje bild till den låda där den hör hemma.

notes: Enlarged and checked on the PDFs: the picture series in Ord, begrepp och berättande (both forms) and in Läsa och skriva ord och meningar (both forms); the student form of Läge, storlek och mönster part 5 (both choices are circles there, the square is a key mark only); the quick-look pictures in Antal 0-10 part 3 A (measured 20 pt and 25 pt boxes); the weekday boxes of Klockan och almanackan in check and key; the odd/even student form of Talen 0-20 (the leftover is framed on the student sheet); the printed words in Ljuda och stava part 5; the word-picture card 'tå'; the bat/duck/reindeer symmetry choice; every row of the four symmetry grids in Geometriska objekt; the right angles and the same-area/same-perimeter rectangles in Fyrhörningar. I counted every picture group, tally, bar and number-line arrow from the sheets.

Tick and cross: no ✓ appears anywhere in these 23 checks. The only marking task ('Säkert, möjligt, omöjligt') asks the child to 'kryssa i en ruta', which is the normal Swedish way to choose on a form; a cross there does not mean wrong. Keep it that way, and keep ✓ out of any Swedish check.

Repeated pattern in directions: many parts with ONE card say 'varje' ('Lyssna på varje räknehändelse', 'Titta på vad som ändras i varje berättelse', 'Dra ett streck från varje figur'). It does not block anything, but where a part has one card the singular reads more naturally; the instruction list gives the singular for the types where it matters most.

Sound tasks in förskoleklass (Språklekar parts 1-3): the teacher page says the teacher reads the word when none is printed, but the direction lines do not; with 'Lyssna när jag säger ordet' in the direction, a child who names the leg 'knä' or the bee 'humla' can no longer go wrong. Words with r before the last consonant (kort, skrivbord) are acceptable for 'last letter' but are best avoided in sound work.

Open question G3-397: a Swedish teacher would not accept 'simma' and 'klättra' under 'gå'. Ord för att gå are promenera, vandra, marschera, traska, lunka, strosa, kliva, stega, trippa, smyga, stappla, lufsa; ord för att titta are kika, glutta, spana, stirra, glo, blänga, betrakta, granska, skåda. 'springa'/'kuta' are running, also not 'gå'.

Titles promising more than the check asks (said honestly in 'Inte med i kunskapskollen' only where a whole lesson is missing): 'hälften' in Talen 0-20 (part 5 asks only doubles), 'adjektiv' in Substantiv, verb och adjektiv (no part asks it), 'årets månader' in Klockan och almanackan part 1, 'rim' in Språklekar.

Small language points for the next pass: 'mangos' (Räknehändelser 0-20 part 4 B) and 'limer' (Läsa, förstå och skriva part 1 B) are everyday plurals that look odd in print; 'Elias räknar 3 fikon' is an odd opening for a förskoleklass story; 'Oscar trampar på sin cykel' can be read as 'steps on his bike'.
Answer-position notes that do not block: Talen 0-20 parts 6 and 7 run udda/jämnt in the same order in A and B; in Ordkunskap part 3 the two right words form a whole row in three of four cards.
